meta.title: Beat Combat Demo
meta.notes: Prototype: 4-beat combat encounter using only scene text + 4 choices per beat. No stats required. Built to drop into VerseCraft-Clean as a test story file.
meta.blurb: A quick 4-beat combat prototype. Make four tactical choices. Your momentum shifts between Advantage, Neutral, and Danger. Win or lose at the end.

S01.text:
A rusted corridor. Flickering light. Your boot scrapes grit and metal as you step around a toppled locker.

A raider steps into view, pipe-blade in hand, grin sharp as broken glass.

There is no time to talk. This is a fast fight: four beats. Each decision changes momentum.

CHOICES

OPENING STRIKE
You hit first. If you land cleanly, you seize the rhythm and control the exchange.

CONTROL THE RANGE
You back-step and angle your body, forcing the raider to commit before you do.

FEINT AND DRAW
You sell a fake weakness to bait a swing, hoping to punish the overreach.

HOLD YOUR GROUND
You plant your feet and brace. Strong if timed right, disastrous if you guess wrong.

S02.text:
ADVANTAGE - BEAT 1

Your first move lands with purpose. The raider flinches and shifts weight backward. You can feel it: you have the tempo.

The corridor is narrow. The locker wreckage limits lateral movement. The raider is breathing harder than they want to admit.

CHOICES

PRESS THE ATTACK
Keep the rhythm. Force them to defend until they make a mistake.

DISARM ATTEMPT
You risk a technical move to strip the pipe-blade away and end this clean.

CREATE SPACE
You step off-line to avoid a counter. Smart, but it gives them room to reset.

TAKE A HIT
You trade pain for position, letting them clip you so you can deliver a bigger blow.

S03.text:
NEUTRAL - BEAT 1

You avoid the worst of the opening exchange, but nothing decisive happens. The raider circles, testing you.

Your breathing is steady. Their eyes keep dropping to your hands. They are looking for a tell.

CHOICES

JAB AND MOVE
Small strikes to probe. You aim to build momentum without committing.

GRAB THE ARM
You shoot for control: wrist, elbow, shoulder. If it sticks, you can turn the tide.

BACKSTEP HARD
You retreat quickly, trying to force a chase and punish the lunge.

SWING WIDE
A big attack. High payoff if it lands, but it risks giving them a clean counter.

S04.text:
DANGER - BEAT 1

Your timing is off. The raider crowds you, pipe-blade scraping sparks off the locker shell as they herd you toward the wall.

Your options narrow fast. You need space, control, or a hard reversal.

CHOICES

DESPERATE SHOVE
You slam forward with your shoulder to disrupt their balance and steal a breath.

ROLL OUT LEFT
You drop low and try to slip past their weapon side. Tight, risky, but possible.

EYE LINE BREAK
You raise an arm and twist your body, breaking their sightline for a half-second.

PANIC SWING
You flail for distance. It might work, but it is exactly what they want you to do.

S05.text:
ADVANTAGE - BEAT 2

You win the exchange. The raider is reacting instead of acting. Their blade hand is late. Their steps are sloppy.

You have a window to end this or set up a clean finish.

CHOICES

TARGET THE HAND
You strike at the weapon hand. Disarm or disable, then finish.

BODY SHOT
You drive into ribs or gut. It breaks their breath and collapses posture.

RESET YOUR FEET
You reposition for safety. You keep control, but you delay the finish.

GO FOR THE HEAD
High risk. High reward. If you miss, you pay for it.

S06.text:
NEUTRAL - BEAT 2

You stabilize. The raider no longer has you pinned, but they are still dangerous.

The corridor hums with electricity and distant machinery. Your senses narrow to motion and breath.

CHOICES

CUT THE ANGLE
You step to the side and force them to turn. Good way to steal momentum.

CLINCH AND KNEE
You close distance and turn it ugly. Works if you get inside the blade.

BAIT THE LUNGE
You offer space, inviting the charge so you can counter.

BACK UP AGAIN
You retreat too much. You risk losing ground and letting them set pace.

S07.text:
DANGER - BEAT 2

A mistake costs you. The raider clips you and you feel heat bloom along your arm. Not deep, but enough.

Your focus spikes. You can still win, but you cannot keep trading damage.

CHOICES

HARD COUNTER
You commit to a sharp counter the moment they swing again.

THROW DEBRIS
You kick grit and scrap up into their face to interrupt.

GO LOW FAST
You attack the legs to topple them. If you fail, you get carved.

FREEZE UP
You hesitate. Hesitation is how people bleed out in corridors like this.

S08.text:
ADVANTAGE - BEAT 3

You are in control now. The raider is backing up into their own mess of shattered metal.

Their grip is failing. Their confidence is gone. One more clean sequence can end it.

CHOICES

LOCK THE ARM
You isolate the weapon arm and twist. Break it, disarm, or both.

SWEEP THE LEGS
You take their base out. If they hit the ground, the fight ends.

LET THEM RUN
You disengage. You keep yourself safe, but you risk them calling friends.

SHOWBOAT HIT
You go for style. Style gets you hurt when luck flips.

S09.text:
NEUTRAL - BEAT 3

The fight stays balanced. You trade position and space. Neither of you fully commits.

The raider is angry now, less careful. That can be a weakness you exploit.

CHOICES

FORCE A CLINCH
You close distance and smother the blade with body control.

SET A TRAP STEP
You lure them into a specific spot and time the counter.

CIRCLE AND WAIT
You stall. Safe, but it gives them time to read you.

CHARGE STRAIGHT
You rush them head-on. Brave, simple, and sometimes exactly wrong.

S10.text:
DANGER - BEAT 3

Your margin is thin. The raider presses hard. Your arm stings. Your foot catches on the locker edge.

This is where you either reverse the fight or you go down.

CHOICES

RIPOSTE NOW
You bet everything on timing. If you land first, the momentum flips.

SHOVE INTO WALL
You slam them into the corridor wall to stall the blade.

DROP AND ROLL
You go low and roll away. It might buy time, but it can also expose you.

TURN YOUR BACK
You try to flee. In a hallway, turning away is asking for the blade.

S11.text:
ADVANTAGE - BEAT 4

Final beat. You have the raider exactly where you want them.

Their weapon hand is compromised. Their stance is broken. The corridor belongs to you.

CHOICES

FINISH CLEANLY
You end it with minimal risk: disarm, strike, done.

KNOCKOUT ONLY
You choose restraint. Drop them without killing.

TAKE THE WEAPON
You secure the pipe-blade as loot before you move on.

WARN AND LEAVE
You make it clear the next move ends them, then you walk.

S12.text:
NEUTRAL - BEAT 4

Final beat. It is still contested, but you are not losing.

One good decision ends it. One sloppy decision turns it into a disaster.

CHOICES

SAFE FINISH
You take the boring win: position first, then strike.

ALL IN STRIKE
You gamble on one big hit to end it instantly.

DISENGAGE NOW
You back away and end the fight without closure.

USE THE ENVIRONMENT
You drive them into debris and use the corridor itself as a weapon.

S13.text:
DANGER - BEAT 4

Final beat. This is bad.

The raider is inside your guard. The pipe-blade flashes. You feel the cold certainty of a wrong choice.

CHOICES

LAST SECOND BLOCK
You try to catch the blade on forearm and bone. It might save you, it might end you.

KICK AND SCRAMBLE
You create space with a brutal kick and hope you can stand before they cut you.

GRAB THE BLADE
A desperate move: hands on steel. Pain for control.

TAKE THE HIT
You accept the strike to keep your feet. Sometimes people do this. Sometimes people die.

S14.text:
WIN

You end it.

The raider collapses, the corridor goes quiet, and your breathing returns to normal. The flicker of the overhead light feels slower now, less threatening.

This is what a four-beat fight looks like when you keep momentum.

CHOICES

RESTART ENCOUNTER
Run it again and test different choices to see how momentum shifts.

END DEMO
Stop here. This is just a prototype story module.

LOAD MENU
If your build routes to menu, use this as your exit.

TRY AGAIN FAST
Same restart, but imagine you are choosing under pressure.

S15.text:
LOSE

The blade wins.

It happens in half a second: steel, impact, your balance leaving you. The corridor tilts. The raider is a silhouette against flickering light.

This is what a four-beat fight looks like when you stay in Danger too long.

CHOICES

RESTART ENCOUNTER
Run it again and test different choices to climb back into control.

END DEMO
Stop here. This is just a prototype story module.

LOAD MENU
If your build routes to menu, use this as your exit.

TRY NEW PATH
Restart and pick different options from the first beat.

S16.text:
RESTART HUB

This scene exists as a hard, obvious anchor so you can verify your runtime can jump cleanly and re-render without leaking prior text.

CHOICES

START OVER
Return to the intro and replay the full four beats.

START FROM ADV
Jump straight into Advantage state for quick testing.

START FROM NEUTRAL
Jump straight into Neutral state for quick testing.

START FROM DANGER
Jump straight into Danger state for quick testing.
